headline: The same shop page with its primitives imported instead of local: every use site loses its fold, and `@yak/solid` drops ninefold while hand-written Solid barely moves.

microbench.why: `vanilla-solid` at 500,000 renders/s and `vanilla` at 235,000 do not care where a class name was declared. `next-yak-css` at 226,000 holds because a css prop resolves fragments at build time regardless of module. `next-yak` at 101,000 loses its fold on every primitive. `yak-solid` at 11,500 loses the same folds at a far higher unit price: 29.8 of its 36.3 ms per render is Solid instantiating eleven components per tile, against 3.04 ms of yak's own work.

autocannon.why: `vanilla-solid` at 361 req/s and `vanilla` at 254 lead; `next-yak` holds 159 with its unfolded wrappers. `yak-solid` at 28 req/s is the suite's lowest, since eleven component instantiations per tile happen inside every request.

attribution.why: `vanilla-solid` at 1.33 ms and `next-yak-css` at 2.19 ms lead, followed by `vanilla` at 2.27 ms. `next-yak` at 4.25 ms books 1.71 ms of lib, up from 0.681 ms when the same primitives were local — that difference is the module boundary priced exactly. `cnfast` at 2.87 ms and `cn` at 3.01 ms are unmoved by the split, as a runtime merger should be. `yak-solid` at 36.3 ms leaves 82% in the framework bucket.

hydrate.why: `next-yak-css` at 57.4 ms, `vanilla` at 58.4 ms and `vanilla-solid` at 59.0 ms tie. `yak-solid` at 301 ms is the case's outlier, walking eleven unfolded wrappers per tile, and `goober` at 260 ms and `styled-components` at 247 ms attach their sheets.

inp.why: `next-yak-css` at 8.4 ms and `vanilla` at 8.5 ms lead. `next-yak` at 22.7 ms shows what unfolded wrappers cost on an update, nearly three times its own css-prop lane. `emotion` at 51.2 ms and `panda-props` at 41.3 ms re-resolve per tile.

mount.why: `vanilla-solid` mounts in 48.2 ms against 128 ms for `vanilla`. `yak-solid` at 227 ms gives that lead away entirely to component instantiation, landing beyond `styled-components` at 210 ms and `goober` at 220 ms.

renderTiming.why: One style recalculation per lane near 0.68 ms, identical to the single-file page. Splitting the source across modules never reaches the style engine.

payload.why: The next-yak css-prop lanes lead at 7,479 gz B with `vanilla` at 7,790 B — byte-identical to the single-file page, since the split changes no output. `yak-solid` is the exception at 26,764 B: 22,123 B of HTML, nearly triple its single-file figure, because each unfolded wrapper opens its own hydration-id namespace and stamps more keys into the markup. `cn` at 29,178 B is unchanged from the single-file page, as its cost is the runtime rather than the layout.

nsweep.why: `vanilla-solid` holds 7.81 ms at the largest size and `vanilla` 18.1 ms. `next-yak` reaches 42.6 ms against 22.2 ms for the single-file page, and `yak-solid` 437 ms against 56.5 ms — the module boundary sets the slope for both compilers, ten times more steeply on Solid.

crossCase: The Example `product-grid` shipped the way a design system ships. `vanilla-solid` moves 599,000 to 500,000 renders/s, which is what the split costs with no compiler involved. `next-yak` moves 195,000 to 101,000: folding only rewrites a usage declared in the same module, so every `Card`, `Badge` and `Title` reverts to a runtime wrapper. `yak-solid` moves 105,000 to 11,500 — the same lost fold, but on Solid each lost fold buys a component with a reactive scope rather than one extra React element.
